strengths: Maps to an exact ontology term and considers a pancreatic epithelial candidate.
weaknesses: No canonical acinar markers (PRSS1, CPA1, CELA3A) are present in the DEG list; top markers ACTA2/DCN/GFRA2 point to stellate/mesenchymal rather than acinar identity.

strengths: Detects muscle-associated signal via ACTA2, HSPB6, JPH2 and includes smooth muscle cell as a rank-2 candidate.
weaknesses: No skeletal muscle myogenic markers (MYOD1, MYOG, DES, TNNT2/TNNI2) are present; the skeletal muscle top1 is unsupported, and the PSC branch is better supported by DCN/GFRA2 in pancreatic context.

clusterProfiler.predicted_cell_type: Pancreatic Stellate Cells (PSC) / Activated Mesenchymal-Like Cells
strengths: Directly uses positive markers ACTA2, DCN, GFRA2, HSPB6 to support activated pancreatic stellate identity; correctly notes absence of acinar/endocrine/ductal markers.
weaknesses: The DEG list is noisy and includes some non-mesenchymal genes (ELF3, CDX1, PMFBP1), so the PSC assignment rests on a subset of the observed markers.

supporting: Positive DEGs ACTA2, DCN, GFRA2, HSPB6, RASL12, JPH2 in cluster_9 support activated pancreatic stellate/mesenchymal identity (PMID 38092774).
No canonical acinar DEGs (PRSS1, CPA1, CELA3A) are present in the original DEG list, so the acinar branch is unsupported.
No skeletal muscle DEGs (MYOD1, MYOG, DES, TNNT2/TNNI2) are present, so the skeletal muscle branch is unsupported.
conflicting: The DEG list also contains ELF3, CDX1, BPIFA3, PMFBP1, PLA2G2E, SPACA1, which are not expected in pancreatic stellate cells and may represent ambient/noise or minor contamination.
Step1 lineage mapping for the original markers is largely 'unknown', so the PSC signature rests on a subset of the DEG list.
enrichment_or_literature: Reactome enrichment terms (Metabolism, Glycosaminoglycan metabolism, Signal Transduction, Interleukin-38 signaling, MyD88/IRAK4 deficiency) are compatible with an activated stromal/inflammatory state.
PMID 38092774 is cited as allowed literature context for the stellate/mesenchymal marker interpretation.
